transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Venture xCard.
Earn unlimited double miles and a $300 annual Capital One travel credit.
Capital One. What's in your wallet? Terms of fly. Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
The British Navy says five oil tankers were struck in major waterways in the Middle East over the weekend.
Commercial ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted
since the U.S. and Israel began attacking Iran more than seven months ago.
NPR's Hadil Al-Shalchi reports.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center, which is run by the British Navy,
said a crew was safe and an investigation was underway
after a commercial tanker reported explosions near the Babel-Mendab Strait.
Babel-Mendab is an alternate waterway on the Red Sea used to transport oil.
Saudi ships have been targeted there by the Iranian-backed Yemeni Houthi rebels.
In separate incidents, four tankers were struck transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday and Sunday,
according to the British organization.
One vessel suffered damage to its engine room.
It was unclear who launched those attacks.
Oil has been flowing more steadily in recent weeks as the U.S. military,
which maintains a blockade of Iranian ports, guides vessels across the strait.
It has yet to recover its pre-war mark.
Hadil Al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
Brazil is heading for a presidential runoff.
The country's president, Luis Nenacio Lula da Silva, will face Flavio Bolsonaro,
the son of Brazil's former far-right leader.
Bolsonaro captured about 47 percent of the vote in yesterday's election.
Lula received 45 percent of the vote.
NPR's Carrie Khan has more from Rio de Janeiro.
Flavio Bolsonaro did very well over Lula,
losing ground in major states around the country.
This was Flavio Bolsonaro's first national election, too.
His father appointed him as the forebearer of the Bolsonaro conservative movement,
and a lot of people were skeptical since he's seen as not as charismatic or skilled as his father.
But he finished ahead of Lula and goes into the runoff with huge political momentum.
Brazil's presidential runoff is set for October 25th.
Today marks the beginning of a new U.S. Supreme Court term,
and PR's Carrie Johnson says the High Court will be examining a case about climate change
stemming from a lawsuit in Boulder, Colorado.
Boulder says Suncor and ExxonMobil deceived the public
about how fossil fuels contributed to global warming.
And now the company should help cover costs the city and county have racked up to respond.
The energy companies say this dispute is too big to leave to state courts to handle.
They'll argue the issue is reserved for the federal government
because of the structure of the U.S. Constitution,
how the Supreme Court decides could short-circuit dozens of cases
in the state courts worth billions of dollars.
Legal experts say the case also could have implications for A.I.
and other sweeping issues that cross state boundaries.
Carrie Johnson, NPR News.
This year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine is supposed to be announced within the hour.
This is NPR News.
Authorities in South Georgia say no arrests have been made
after gunfire broke out at an outdoor homecoming party in the town of Vienna.
Two people were killed, more than 30 others were injured early yesterday,
some by gunfire. Several people were critically hurt.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee says former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton
will lead an investigation into last week's failed execution
of death row inmate Christa Gail Pike.
Mariana Bacaiau with member station WPLN has more from Nashville.
Lee called for the third party review after last week's botched execution left Christa Pike
in critical condition but alive at a local hospital.
The current lethal injection process was developed after Stanton's last review
found problems with how the state inspected the drugs it uses to carry out the death penalty.
Lee says Stanton's investigation will determine if the current protocol was followed
and evaluate its effectiveness from there.
In the meantime, the governor has called off the remaining execution scheduled for this year.
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bacaiau in Nashville.
Fuel prices in the U.S. have declined over the last week.
AAA says the cost of regular gasoline and diesel have each dropped more than 10 cents a gallon.
Regular is now averaging about $4.36 nationwide.
Diesel has declined to $6.32.
AAA says prices at the pumps have dropped because of declines in oil prices.
Undefeated Texas remains number one in this week's Associated Press top 25 college football rankings.
The Longhorns are followed by Georgia at number two, then Notre Dame, Miami, and Ohio State.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.

Brazil heads to presidential runoff between President Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro in October
Supreme Court begins new term, will examine climate change lawsuit from Boulder Colorado
Two killed, over 30 injured in gunfire at homecoming party in Vienna Georgia
Tennessee Governor Lee appoints Ed Stanton to investigate failed execution of Christa Pike
U.S. fuel prices decline, regular gasoline averaging $4.36 and diesel at $6.32 nationally
